Periapical abscess: The patient has a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, with fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area. The presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa and the lack of tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth suggest a periapical abscess.

The patient's symptoms of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, are consistent with a periapical abscess. The panoramic radiography demonstrating a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices further supports this diagnosis.
Periapical granuloma: The patient's symptoms and examination findings, including the presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, are consistent with a periapical granuloma. The provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma was made based on the clinical presentation and radiographic findings.

The patient's symptoms and the presence of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa could also be indicative of a periapical granuloma. The histopathological examination of the gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue obtained from the curettage may provide further evidence for this diagnosis.
